text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Kabariti tells Hamas through the Islamic Action Front (IAF) that King Hussein will bring up their jailed leader Abu Marzook's case with U.S. President Clinton during the monarch's coming visit to Washington.
- Sources say Jordan will allow Abu Marzook, who is now jailed in the U.S., to reside as a normal citizen.
- Crown Prince Hassan says Europe ready to support Arabs on the two issues of Jerusalem's occupied status and Palestinian refugees.
- An internal debate rages within Islamist ranks on whether they should join the government; the government has succeeded in splitting their ranks.
- Moslem Brotherhood deny there are any discussions with the government to participate in the next government.
- Trade minister says a national team will be set up to prepare a national economic strategy.
- Stocks continue their rise to new highs and turnover rises 82 percent in a week.
- Nigerian fraud gangs renew their activities in Jordan, businessmen say.
- Ministries and public bodies are instructed to submit their projects tenders soon to allow their implementation in the present fiscal year.
- Regent reiterates Jordan's rejection of Israeli claim to all of Jerusalem as capital.
